title: Blank Canvas: My So-Called Artist's Journey
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Akiko Higashimura's autobiographical manga follows her from a cocky high-school student who wants to be a manga artist to a working professional. Her rural art teacher, Kenzou Hidaka, is harsh, temperamental and swings a bamboo sword, yet he pours himself into her training. Looking back as an adult, Akiko weighs how she drifted from his lessons and what she owes him.
life_message: A good life is built by daily, honest work at your craft and by honoring the teachers who believed in you before it is too late.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Pride and face matter to young Akiko, but conflicts are resolved through work, not confrontation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hidaka's strict daily drawing regime is the path to growth.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Teacher-student bond rivals family ties; Akiko's parents also support her.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Sensei's authority is total and the story affirms deference to him.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Classical drawing discipline beside a modern manga career.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Art as self-expression, but hard work and earning a living come first.

folkways.japan: The sensei's absolute authority and the student's lifelong debt reflect Japanese teacher-student (shitei) norms, along with the art-school entrance exam culture.

delivery.evidence: Autobiography looks back on a teacher with regret (AniList Autobiographical, Non-fiction); no source comments on delivery (to verify)

delivery.note: The author's adult narration reflects on what she owes her teacher, so the lesson is framed as memoir.

winners_losers: Akiko succeeds as an artist, but the story gives its sympathy to Hidaka, whose unselfish teaching she repaid too late.
